title: Preparation of cerium oxide/graphene oxide composite aerogels and its photocatalytic activity for Congo red
content: The CeO2/GO composite aerogels were fabricated through a straightforward one-step hydrothermal process, specifically designed for the photocatalytic breakdown of Congo red. By integrating CeO2 with GO, the material's specific surface area is significantly boosted, its band gap narrowed, and its photocatalytic performance notably enhanced. The aerogel exhibits a mesoporous structure with an 8 nm average pore diameter and a remarkable surface area of 93.88 m2 g−1. Furthermore, the aerogel exhibits exceptional dye degradation selectivity, especially with Congo red, where it achieves a photocatalytic degradation rate of up to 80.32%. The inclusion of GO plays a pivotal role in creating vacancy defects within CeO2 and promoting the efficient separation of photogenerated charge carriers. Compared to pure CeO2, the bandgap of the CeO2/GO composite aerogels is reduced by 36%, leading to enhanced catalytic performance under visible light.
